## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a printed card for a City Planner / Local Authority
reader, with two maps (map 01: signed GeoSensitivity, rank-1 LSOA outlined; map 02:
built-environment share of each LSOA's local importance). This section replaces section 14
"Length and form" and its bolding rule. Every other section, including prohibited claims and
the self-check, still applies.

Plain language for this reader overrides the section 9 priority on clustering statistics:
do not cite Moran's I, p-values, LISA class names, coefficients or other test statistics.
Say what the model relies on, and where, in words a planner uses. Shares, percentages and
ranks are fine.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words: the single most decision-relevant finding
  that answers user_question.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters, e.g. "1/168", "14%"); label is at most 6 words saying what
  the figure is and where. Choose the four figures a planner should remember.
- "section_01": at most 60 words, about map 01: which areas matter most to the model (the
  rank-1 GeoSensitivity LSOA and the next highest, by locality name), and what the model
  relies on in the rank-1 LSOA (its crime-history and built-environment shares, and the
  leading built feature).
- "section_02": at most 65 words, about map 02: what the model relies on across Hull by
  feature category (hull_feature_category_shares), which built-environment features carry
  that category's share (hull_built_feature_shares), and the highest-share LSOAs with their
  leading built feature.
- "footer": one limitation, at most 15 words.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite in headline and sections as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: exactly 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section, each at most 4 words
  (the finding phrase itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before
  answering, count the [[t:...]] spans in headline, section_01 and section_02 and fix any
  count outside these ranges;
- no other markup and no markdown bold. Tiles and footer carry no markup.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON.

illustrative_narrative.headline: The model depends most on [[t:Old Town]], but leans on built-environment features in [[t:residential areas]] instead.
illustrative_narrative.section_01: The model depends most on [[t:Old Town]] (029E, rank [[n:1/168]]), well ahead of Dairycoates and Sculcoates. There it leans on [[t:recent crime history]] ([[n:83%]] of its local importance); built-environment features carry only [[n:6%]], mostly [[t:retail]].
illustrative_narrative.section_02: Across Hull the model relies mainly on [[t:crime history]] ([[n:61%]]), then census population characteristics ([[n:20%]]); built-environment features carry [[n:14%]], led by retail, green space and roads. They matter most in [[t:residential areas]] ([[n:41-45%]]): Longhill, Avenues and Sculcoates on [[t:green space]], Bilton Grange on intersections, Orchard Park on transit stops.
illustrative_narrative.footer: Model behaviour, not planning targets or causes of crime.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch area-data SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA replaces all of its model inputs with Hull training medians, and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (area-data design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.
global_spatial_pattern.lisa_counts_unit: number of LSOAs in each LISA class, not number of clusters

evaluation.att_stability_note: Controlled-input ATT stability. Distinct from multi-run Consistency.

consistency.definition: Multi-run explanation consistency across seeds (consistency_seed_base=100). Pairwise Rank Spearman, Score Pearson, and Top-20% Jaccard of |coefficients|. Not controlled-input ATT stability.

geo_design.name: area_data
geo_design.definition: Area-data design: masking an LSOA replaces ALL of its model inputs with the training median; response is Wasserstein-1 on the affected LSOA-month predictions of the 30-feature model; LSOAs ranked by the signed Geo-SMILE coefficient.

evidence.user_question: Which areas matter most to the model, and where does it rely on built-environment features, and which ones?

built_environment_share.definition: Share of each LSOA's total local Feature importance (|local coefficient| summed over all 30 Feature players) that comes from the 12 built-environment players: area, nightlife, retail, transit stops, roads, intersections, green space (count and density variants pooled). It is a share of model attribution, not an effect on crime.
built_environment_share.hull_share_note: Hull-wide shares pool |local coefficient| over all 168 LSOAs; categories sum to 1.
built_environment_share.limitation: Attribution shares describe model behaviour; they are not planning targets.

content.headline: The model relies most on [[t:Old Town]], but built-environment features matter most in [[t:Longhill]] and similar areas.
content.section_01: The model is most sensitive to [[t:Old Town]] (029E, rank [[n:1/168]]), ahead of Dairycoates and Sculcoates. In Old Town, [[t:recent crime history]] dominates ([[n:83%]] of local importance); built-environment features contribute only [[n:6%]], mainly [[t:retail]].
content.section_02: Across Hull, the model relies mainly on [[t:crime history]] ([[n:61%]]), then census characteristics ([[n:20%]]); built-environment features account for [[n:14%]], led by retail, green space, and roads. Built features matter most in [[t:Longhill]] ([[n:45%]], green space), Avenues, Sculcoates, Bilton Grange (intersections), and Orchard Park (transit stops).
content.footer: Attribution shares show model behaviour, not planning targets.
